authors: Sami Baral, Li Lucy, Ryan Knight, Alice Ng, Luca Soldaini, Neil Heffernan, Kyle Lo
selection_note: Small candidate set selected from teacher captions; source images are unmodified and include the printed problem beside the student response. Captions and visual screening are not numerical ground truth.

cases.candidate_use: Multiple hand-drawn lines; unlabeled numerical axes
cases.inspection_status: visually screened; not yet tested in STAR
cases.visual_notes: Two pencil lines on photographed graph paper; numerical axis labels are absent; image is dim and skewed.

cases.candidate_use: Drawn lines and written equation labels disagree, according to teacher caption
cases.inspection_status: visually screened; not yet tested in STAR
cases.visual_notes: Two shallow lines on photographed grid paper with handwritten equation labels that indicate a different slope; source includes a black redaction box.

cases.candidate_use: Proportional graph whose student line misses the origin, according to teacher caption
cases.inspection_status: visually screened; not yet tested in STAR
cases.visual_notes: Connected plotted points rise from the first nonzero point; the visible student line does not extend to the origin.

cases.candidate_use: Mixed rising, curved, and flat sections
cases.inspection_status: visually screened; not yet tested in STAR
cases.visual_notes: Small, low-contrast student photograph contains a rising section, a rounded peak, and a nearly horizontal section.

cases.candidate_use: Incomplete graph with sparse points and shadows; check that recognition does not invent missing geometry
cases.inspection_status: visually screened; not yet tested in STAR
cases.visual_notes: Photographed hand-drawn grid has sparse plotted points and strong shadows; a complete connected curve is not clearly visible. Useful as an incomplete-input case.

cases.candidate_use: Hand-drawn graph on grid paper with numerical scales
cases.inspection_status: visually screened; not yet tested in STAR
cases.visual_notes: Photographed grid-paper graph has multiple straight segments and a sharp peak, labeled axes, and numerical scales.
